<h1 class="profile-name" id="elisa-fazzari">Elisa Fazzari</h1>

<p class="profile-subtitle">Cosmology &amp; university teaching</p>

I am a cosmologist with a **PhD in Astronomy, Astrophysics and Space Science** from the joint programme of Sapienza University of Rome and the University of Rome Tor Vergata. I study what observations of the expanding Universe can tell us about **dark energy, gravity and the Hubble tension**.

I enjoy helping students work through the same questions that drive my research: how to turn a physical idea into a model, test it against data and understand what the result can tell us. At Sapienza, I have taught undergraduate mathematics and led practical sessions in Bayesian inference for Master’s and PhD students.

[Research projects](projects.qmd) · [Teaching and mentoring](tutoring.qmd)

## Research interests

- **Late-time cosmic acceleration.** I test models of dynamical dark energy and modified gravity against observations, including Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations and cosmic chronometers.
- **Cosmography and the Hubble tension.** I develop ways to reconstruct the expansion history from data with minimal assumptions about the underlying dynamics.
- **Scientific computing and inference.** I build reusable Python workflows for Bayesian parameter estimation, including Cobaya pipelines and numerical checks. I have also used genetic algorithms to explore modified-gravity models.
- **Early-Universe physics.** I have studied the background evolution and observational constraints of $f(R)$ inflation.

[Publications](publications.qmd) · [Talks and posters](talks.qmd)

## Academic background

- **PhD in Astronomy, Astrophysics and Space Science**, Sapienza University of Rome and University of Rome Tor Vergata, awarded 6 November 2026. My doctoral research examined dark energy and cosmological tensions under the supervision of Alessandro Melchiorri and Giovanni Montani.
- **Visiting researcher**, Instituto de Física Teórica (IFT UAM–CSIC), Madrid, April–June 2026. I worked with Savvas Nesseris on testing modified gravity with genetic algorithms.
- **Visiting researcher**, University of Sheffield, March 2024 and March 2025. I worked with William Giarè and Eleonora Di Valentino on late-time cosmology and cosmography. The first visit was supported by a COST Action CosmoVerse Short-Term Scientific Mission grant.
- **MSc in Astronomy and Astrophysics** and **BSc in Physics**, Sapienza University of Rome (2023 and 2021, both 110/110 cum laude).
